newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks rebound to close sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks rebound to close sharply higher.

text.p: Toronto stocks ended sharply higher on Monday as investors jumped back into Canada's biggest stock market following last week's sell off.
The TSE 300 Composite Index rebounded 96.48 points to close at 5906.54 in brisk turnover of 80.4 million shares worth C$1.16 billion ($858 million).
The key index sank about 3.4 percent last week following comments by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan, which spooked financial markets worldwide.
The TSE's recovery was aided by a strong rally in Canadian bonds which outperformed U.S. treasuries on Monday.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose 1.20 to C$112.25 to yield 6.979 percent on widespread buying following the bond market's biggest one-day loss last Thursday and further losses on Friday.
Stock analysts said the upcoming RRSP (registered retirement savings plan) season should give the TSE momentum to move higher over the next few weeks.

"Mutual funds are going to be in the markets now to build their positions," said Jim Doak, investment research director at ScotiaMcLeod Inc. In today's action, advancing issues outpaced declines 636 to 374, with 275 stocks unchanged.
* Conglomerates, banking, transportation and consumer products led Monday's rally. Laidlaw Inc. class B was the top transport issue, up 0.60 at 16.50 on 1.5 million shares.
* Among the high-flying banks, Royal Bank of Canada jumped 1.15 to 48.40. Toronto-Dominion Bank gained 1.30 to 34.55.
* BioChem Pharma Inc. soared 5.70 to 65.70 after the company said it expected sales of its anit-AIDS drug 3TC to double in 1997 to C$600 million ($443 million).
* Bre-X Minerals Ltd. led active issues, falling 0.10 to 20.05 on 1.8 million shares.
